title: 〜は〜です
notes: Connects a topic (は, read wa) to a noun or description. The polite negative is じゃありません; the plain form is だ.

title: 〜か
notes: Adding か at the end of a sentence turns it into a question. In speech it can be shown with a rising tone. In casual talk か is often dropped and only the rising tone remains.

examples.ja: 明日、学校に{{行きますか}}。
examples.en: Will you go to school tomorrow?

title: 〜も
notes: も replaces は, が, or を when the item is also true or included. Do not add は after も; も already marks the topic. It can attach to nouns, verbs, and adjectives.

title: 〜の
notes: の links two nouns: the first owns or describes the second. At the end of a casual sentence, の can soften a statement or express a feeling.

examples.ja: {{日本の}}食べ物はおいしいです。
これは{{田中さんの}}かさです。

title: 〜を
meaning: marks the direct object of an action
notes: を marks the thing a transitive verb acts on. It is written as を but pronounced o. Intransitive verbs such as 行く or 来る use に or へ for direction instead.

examples.ja: 毎朝{{コーヒーを}}飲みます。

title: 〜に
structure: Time に Verb / Place に 行きます
notes: に marks a specific point in time (七時に, 月曜日に) and the goal of movement (学校に). Do not use に with きのう, きょう, あした, or いつ. Those time words take no particle.

title: 〜で（場所）
meaning: at / in (place where an action happens)
notes: で after a place shows where an action takes place. It is different from に, which marks where something exists or where one is going. Use で with verbs of action such as 勉強する or 食べる.

examples.en: I wait for a friend at the station.

title: 〜で（手段）
notes: で after a noun shows the tool, means of transport, or language used to do something. The same particle marks a place of action, so context decides. For accompanying people use と, not で.

title: 〜と（〜と一緒に）
notes: と after a person means doing something together with that person. It is different from the list particle と, which joins nouns. Use と with 友だち, 家族, and similar people.

examples.en: I watch a movie with my friend.
I go shopping with my mother.
I talk with my older brother.

title: 〜と（並列）
notes: と joins nouns into a list that is complete. For a partial list use や instead, which implies there are others. と can only link nouns, not verbs or adjectives.

examples.ja: {{りんごと}}バナナが好きです。
{{ペンと}}ノートを買いました。
examples.en: I bought a pen and a notebook.

title: 〜から〜まで
meaning: from ... to ... (range in time or place)
structure: Start から End まで
notes: から marks the starting point and まで the end point. Either one can be used alone, as in 九時から or 駅まで. Do not replace まで with に here.

examples.ja: {{九時から五時まで}}働きます。
examples.en: I work from nine to five.

examples.ja: {{東京から大阪まで}}新幹線で行きます。
examples.en: I go from Tokyo to Osaka by bullet train.

examples.ja: {{月曜日から金曜日まで}}学校があります。
examples.en: There is school from Monday to Friday.

title: 〜が（主語）
meaning: marks the subject of a sentence
notes: が marks the new or focused subject, especially with 誰, どれ, and with existence verbs. は introduces a topic, が points to the doer. Some sentences with 好き or 上手 also take が for the object of feeling.

title: 〜が好き／上手／下手
structure: Noun が 好きです / 上手です / 下手です
notes: 好き, 上手, and 下手 take が for the thing liked or the skill, not を. 嫌い uses the same pattern. Use these with nouns or with 〜こと when the item is a verb phrase.

title: 〜がある／いる
meaning: there is / there are (things / living things)
structure: Place に Noun が あります / います
notes: ある is for things and plants, いる is for people and animals. The location takes に, and the thing that exists takes が. The plain forms are ある and いる.
detect: が(ある|あります|いる|います)

examples.ja: 机の上にペン{{があります}}。
examples.en: There is a pen on the desk.
There is a cat in the garden.
There is milk in the fridge.

title: 〜ましょう
notes: ましょう suggests doing something together. A common reply is はい、そうしましょう. For a polite offer of help, use 〜ましょうか instead.

title: 〜ませんか
meaning: would you like to ...? / shall we ...?
notes: ませんか invites someone politely to do something. It is softer than a direct request. Use it with people you do not know well, and accept or decline with はい、ぜひ or すみません.

examples.en: Would you like to watch a movie?
Would you like to go tomorrow?

examples.ja: 一緒に{{昼ご飯を食べませんか}}。
examples.en: Would you like to eat lunch together?

title: 〜たい
structure: Verb stem たい / たいです
notes: たい attaches to the verb stem and works like an i-adjective. The object takes を or が, and both are seen in speech. Use it only for your own wishes; for someone else's wish use 〜たがっている.

examples.en: I want to go to Japan.

examples.ja: ケーキを{{食べたい}}です。

title: 〜に行く
structure: Verb stem に 行きます
notes: The verb stem before に expresses the purpose of going. The sentence ends with a movement verb such as 行く, 来る, or 帰る. Nouns before に are the thing being done, like 買い物に行く.
detect: に行(く|きます|きましょう)

examples.en: I am going to see a movie.

examples.ja: ラーメンを{{食べに行きましょう}}。

title: 〜ています
structure: Verb て-form いる / ています
notes: ている shows an action in progress or a repeated state. With some verbs such as 知る or 持つ it shows a resulting state. The plain form is 〜ている and the polite form is 〜ています.

examples.en: I am reading a book now.

examples.hint: 勉強する + ています

title: 〜てください
notes: てください politely asks someone to do something. It is a direct request, so add ね or すみません to soften it.

examples.ja: ここに名前を{{書いてください}}。
ゆっくり{{話してください}}。

title: 〜ないでください
structure: Verb ない-form で ください
notes: ないでください politely asks someone not to do something. It is the negative counterpart of 〜てください. Use it for rules, warnings, or polite requests to stop.

examples.ja: ここは{{入らないでください}}。
examples.hint: 入る + ないでください

examples.ja: ここで{{写真を撮らないでください}}。
examples.hint: 撮る + ないでください
忘れる + ないでください

title: 〜てもいい
meaning: may / it is okay to (do something)
notes: てもいい gives or asks permission. Asking 〜てもいいですか is polite. Do not use it to refuse: for a prohibition use 〜てはいけない, and for it not being necessary use 〜なくてもいい.

examples.ja: ここで写真を{{撮ってもいい|撮ってもよい}}ですか。
今日は{{休んでもいい}}です。
examples.en: You may take the day off today.

title: 〜てはいけない
meaning: must not / is not allowed to (do something)
structure: Verb て-form はいけない / はいけません
notes: てはいけない states a prohibition. It is firm, so use it for rules or to warn someone. Speakers often say ちゃいけない in casual talk. The polite form is 〜てはいけません.

examples.ja: ここでたばこを{{吸ってはいけません}}。
examples.hint: 吸う + てはいけない

examples.ja: 学校に{{遅れてはいけない}}。
examples.en: You must not be late for school.
examples.hint: 遅れる + てはいけない

examples.ja: プールで{{走ってはいけません}}。
examples.en: You must not run in the pool.
examples.hint: 走る + てはいけない

title: 〜から（理由）
notes: から gives a reason and comes after the cause, as in 寒いから. The result comes after the comma. It is more direct than ので, which sounds softer and more polite.

examples.ja: 雨が降っている{{から}}、行きません。
examples.en: Because it's raining, I won't go.
I can't come because I'm busy.

examples.ja: {{寒いから}}、窓を閉めてください。
examples.en: It's cold, so please close the window.
